newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps edge higher with mogas pack leader.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps edge higher with mogas pack leader.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly steady to stronger on Wednesday as crude futures consolidated and then built upon Tuesday's gains.
Gasoline swaps gained $5 or so as U.S.-driven demand kicked in after API data showed stocks dropping 2.8 million barrels.
Brent crude CFDs were steady on the close-in dates and several cents stronger further out while naphtha put on $1 or so.
Heavy fuel was steady, but low sulphur swaps eased back $1-1.50.

Dealers said gasoline swaps were pushed higher by the strong U.S. interest in physical product and that August was valued around $193.75, against $188.75 on Tuesday. September traded at $187.00 earlier in the day and was pegged around $188.50 towards the close.
Brent CFDs were fairly flat close in with July 23-25 hovering around +9 cents against September Brent from +10 cents while July 28-01 was put at +8/9 cents against September compared with +6/7 cents.
August 4-8 firmed to -5 cents against September compared with -13/14 cents while August 11-15 firmed to -12 cents from -17/18 cents.
A July 28-August 1 CFD traded at September + 9 cents while August 4-8 was done twice, once at September -4 cents and once at September -7 cents.
An August 4-8 to 11-15 roll was done at +7 cents while a August 11-15 to 18-22 roll went at + 3 cents.

Heavy fuel swaps were steady in August and marginally firmer further out. August traded a couple of times at $89.25 with September 50-75 cents contangoed. Some dealers saw a push in the physical barge market to break higher from $90 fob.
The high-low fuel spread eased back a touch as low sulphur swaps bucked the general market trend by slipping slightly. August was thought to have traded twice at $94.50, about $1 off.
Naphtha was about $1 stronger with August tradeing at $185.50 and September going at $184.00.
